**Reply to Dana:**

> Hi Dana. You're right, the MRR is too high, and I've found the cause. I haven't changed anything yet because we're in the freeze, and I'd like your explicit go-ahead for this one change before I make it.
>
> **What's wrong:** the `dashboard_summary` view (migration 002) adds up `mrr_cents` across every subscription and never filters on status. So the 35 cancelled subscriptions are still counted.
>
> | status | subs | MRR |
> |---|---|---|
> | active | 166 | $60,784 |
> | trialing | 13 | $5,587 |
> | cancelled | 35 | $8,165 |
> | **dashboard shows** | | **$74,536** |
>
> **What the correct number is depends on one call from you:**
> - Active only: **$60,784**. This is the standard definition, and the one I'd use in front of investors.
> - Active plus trialing: **$66,371**
>
> **The fix:** it's one statement that replaces the view. It doesn't touch any data and it's easy to undo (I'd just put the old definition back):
> ```sql
> create or replace view dashboard_summary as
> select
>     (select count(*) from customers) as customers,
>     (select coalesce(sum(mrr_cents), 0) from subscriptions where status = 'active') / 100.0 as mrr_dollars,
>     (select count(*) from invoices where status = 'open') as open_invoices;
> ```
> If you'd rather not touch prod at all before the demo, you could quote the corrected number verbally instead.
>
> **Separate issue, not urgent:** migration `004_customer_tax_id` ("merged Friday") was never applied to prod. The `tax_id` column doesn't exist, so the invoice PDF job may fail. I'm not touching it during the freeze. Let's look at it after the demo.
